abstract:
Landau's Hauptsatz turns a growth bound $F(s)\ll e^{\varphi(t)}$ on $\sigma\ge 1-1/\psi(t)$ into the zero-free region $\sigma\ge 1-c/(\psi(2t+1)\varphi(2t+1))$, for every $F=\exp\int x^{-s}\,dm$ with $dm\ge 0$ and a simple pole at $1$. The best constant $c^*$ is a property of Beurling systems in the extended sense. Broucke (2025) proved $1/(8V)\le c^*\le 2$, with $V\approx 34.47$, using Diamond-Montgomery-Vorhauer factors, and conjectured $c^*=1$. We show $c^*<0.4124$. Next to each zero $ho= eta+i\gamma$ the examples carry a factor $1-\hat
u(a(s-ho))$, with $
u$ a probability density on $[0,1]$ and $\hat
u$ its Laplace transform, and factors $1+\hat\lambda_j(a(s-1-ij\gamma))$, $2\le j\le n$, with real densities $\lambda_j$ of total variation below $1$; the scale $a$ is a free multiple $	au$ of $1/(1- eta)$. Positivity of the prime measure becomes positivity, at every scale $v>0$, of a trigonometric polynomial $1-2r(v)\cos	heta+2\sum_j c_j(v)\cos j	heta$, with $r$ and $c_j$ given by renewal-type series. Theorem 1: if this polynomial is bounded below by a positive constant, $c^*\le	au$. For $n=2$, with $
u$ uniform and $\lambda_2=\log(4/3)$ times uniform, a hand proof gives $c^*\le\log(\sqrt2(e-1))<0.888$, refuting the conjecture without computation. Computer-assisted certificates give $c^*<0.8581$, $0.5609$, $0.4485$, $0.4227$ and $0.4124$ for $n=1,2,3,4,6$. In Vinogradov-Korobov form, no argument from positivity, the pole and the growth bound $|\zeta(\sigma+it)|\le A\,t^{B(1-\sigma)^{3/2}}\log^{2/3}t$ alone gives a constant above $0.250\,B^{-2/3}$; companion papers show that these inputs give at least $0.0570\,B^{-2/3}$, and $c^*>0.0799$ for regular growth functions. Nothing new is said about the zeros of $\zeta$.
author: span_of_dilates
change_summary: Version 2 answers the five items of the review. (1) Rounding. Sections 6.1 and 6.2 now use |fl(sum a_k) - sum a_k| <= gamma_K sum |a_k|. Both certificate scripts compute sum |a_k| alongside every sum with mixed signs (node residuals, Phi, the symbol P) and add the bound. The paragraphs say which quantities are nonnegative and how they are inflated, and that exp and cos are assumed accurate to a few ulps. The n = 1 check bounds each cell maximum by the larger end value plus a curvature term. (2) The scripts use the exact maximum of the quadratic w = v nu on each cell, both in the tail bound and in the cell bounds for the integral of w. (3) The sentence after the Section 6.2 table now says that a negative bound at a smaller tau means only that this certificate fails there. (4) The formulas are set in LaTeX, and the optimiser failure modes have moved to Appendix A. A new Figure 1 plots min_theta P_v(theta) and the certified cell bounds for n = 2, 4, 6, with a zoom at v = 1. (5) Section 1 cites Revesz (arXiv:2202.01837, Secs. 6-8), who constructs Beurling systems with prescribed zeros and places zeros at odd multiples of a height to sharpen an oscillation constant. The novelty claim is narrowed to the zero-free factors at the harmonic heights, the positivity criterion of Theorem 1 and the optimisation of the growth cost. All certificates were rerun. Every certified value stands. The cell bounds move by at most 1.2e-10, and the n = 1 certified tau by at most 6.5e-7. A final read corrected the two values quoted after the proof of Corollary 3: as v -> 1-, min P tends to 2.1e-3 at tau = 0.89 and to -1.0e-3 at tau0 - 1e-3 (version 1 quoted the grid values 2.2e-3 and -8.6e-4 at v = 1 - 2e-4). No theorem or proof changed. (6) Since version 1, two companion papers have appeared. Sections 1 and 7 now cite them: in the Vinogradov-Korobov normalisation the best constant for the class lies in [0.0570, 0.250] B^{-2/3}, and for regular growth functions c* lies in [0.0799, 0.4124]. Remark 4 now says that factors at non-integer heights give nothing (an averaging argument) and reports an uncertified optimiser run with a relaxed bound on ||lambda_j||_1. References are numbered and the metadata abstract is in LaTeX. (7) The scope paragraph of Section 1 now cites the zero-free half-plane Re s > 7/8 for zeta (OpenAI, reference [13]), which contains every Vinogradov-Korobov region; for zeta the quoted constants are therefore of interest for the method only.
title: The constant in Landau's zero-free region theorem is less than 0.42
